1 CRM-W-281 of 2022 & CRM-W-602 of 2022 The brief facts of the case are that Sanjay Gupta and Rajesh Gupta filed criminal writ petition No.12055 of 2021 with prayer for issuance of direction to the respondents for protecting their lives and liberty and 1 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:032479 safeguarding their property.

In the said criminal writ petition, the petitioners therein pleaded that they were working directors of Real Height Developers Pvt. Ltd. GT Road Panipat and that initially 5 Directors namely Shiv Charan Gupta, Attar Chand Gupta, Manish Mittal, Ankur Mittal and Prashant Kumar Mittal were having 75% shares and petitioners therein namely Sanjay Gupta and Rajesh Gupta were having 25% shares in the company.

entities.text: Real Height Developers Pvt. Ltd. GT Road Panipat
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: That Attar Chand Gupta and his sons Ankur Mittal and Manish Mittal owned approximately 13 Bighas of land in the area of village Shimla Maulana District Panipat.
Prashant Mittal son of Shiv Charan Gupta owned approximately 37 Bighas, 16 Biswa, 10 Biswasi of land in the same village.
The aforesaid persons got registered the sale of said land measuring 50 Bigha, 16 Biswa, 10 Biswasi through different sale deeds in name of the Company.
Thus the Company became owner in possession of the said land.

Shiv Charan Gupta, Attar Chand Gupta, Ankur Mittal, Manish Mittal and Prashant Mittal entered into an MoU dated 07.2.2018 (Annexure P-2) whereby they sold their entire rights in the abovesaid land owned by the Company and their respective shares against total consideration of `30 crores in favour of Sanjay Gupta, Rajesh Gupta and one Naresh Kumar and since then the company and its management vested in Rajesh Gupta and Sanjay Gupta while Attar Chand, Manish Mittal, Ankur Mittal, Shiv Charan Gupta and Prashant Kumar Mittal withdrew themselves from the management of the company vide board resolution dated 7.2.2018 (Annexure P-3).
That since then the entire business of the Company is being controlled and managed by Rajesh Gupta and Sanjay Gupta.
That before the filing of the 2 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:032479 petition the opposite party tried to interfere in the management and day to day working of the Company.
Resultantly the petition was filed.

The notice of the said petition was issued to the respondents therein, all of whom were Officers/
Officials of the Government of Haryana.
The State counsel had put in appearance on behalf of the said respondents and pleaded no objection if necessary directions are given to the concerned authorities.

In view of the above, CRWP-12055 of 2021 was disposed of vide order dated 22.12.2021 by this Court in following terms:-
"The present petition is hereby disposed with direction to Superintendent of Police,
Panipat-respondent No.4 to ensure that there will be no interference from any other person into the business and working of the petitioners as well as Real Heights Developers Pvt. Ltd. GT Road Panipat near Eldeco outer gate GT road Panipat"
CRM-W 281 of 2022 has been filed by applicant Attar Chand Gupta with the prayer to modify/
clarify the aforesaid order dated 22.12.2021.

The counsel for the applicant has submitted that the petitioners Sanjay Gupta and Rajesh Gupta did not approach this Court with clean hands and they suppressed the material facts and procured the aforesaid concessional order dated 22.12.2021.

The counsel for the petitioner has further submitted Sanjay Gupta And Anr vs State Of Haryana And Others on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122346913/
2 that actually M/s Real Height Developers Private Limited was incorporated on 07.09.2013 and Attar Chand Gupta, Manish Mittal, Ankur Mittal, Shiv Charan Mittal, Parshant Mittal, Sanjay Gupta and Rajesh 3 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:032479 Gupta are Directors of the said Company.

sentences.text:
That applicant and his family owned 10.58 acres of land in village Shimla Maulana District Panipat and the same was registered in the name of Company vide registered sale deeds dated 09.10.2014,
17.11.2014, 02.02.2015, 06.01.2016 and 06.02.2017.

The petitioners' share was calculated as Rs.8 crores towards the payment of sale consideration of the said land and accordingly they executed an affidavit dated 03.08.2017 in favour of the applicant and they also issued post dated cheques of an amount of Rs.8 crores in discharge of their liability and the amount was agreed to be paid in two yearly installments along with interest @ 1.15 %.
The copy of affidavit is Annexure A-2, having details of the post dated cheques.

Thereafter, MoU dated 07.02.2018 was executed between the petitioners and applicant as per which the petitioner agreed to buy out the shares of applicant and his brother and their sons and the copy of the said MoU is Annexure A-3 and the copies of the concerned resolutions dated 07.02.2018 are Annexures A-4 to A-10.
The aforesaid post dated cheques on their presentation were dishonoured with remarks 'insufficient funds' and consequently complaint under Section 138 N.I. Act is filed against the petitioners.

Further, the petitioners stopped paying the installments as per the terms and conditions of MoU, Annexure A-3 and then applicant issued a legal notice dated 22.02.2020 and thereafter he filed civil suit for recovery of Rs.60 crores but the same was lateron withdrawn on 11.11.2021 as the learned trial Court directed the applicant to fix ad-valorem Court fees.

The applicant also filed complaint before Superintendent of Police,
Panipat but after due enquiry the same was ordered to be filed on 13.05.2021.
Thereafter, the applicant filed another civil suit for recovery of Rs.45 crores against the 4 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:032479 petitioners, which is pending in the Court concerned.

In the meantime,
the petitioner approached this Court and on 22.12.2021 the order sought to be clarified herein was passed.

That on 01.01.2022, FIR No.6 under Section 406, 420 IPC was registered in Police Station Sadar, Panipat against the petitioners on the basis of complaint lodged by the applicant with regard to forgery and cheating committed by the petitioners in regard to MoU dated 07.02.2018.

The counsel for the applicant has further contended that applicant and his brother and their sons are having vested rights in the affairs of Real Height Developers Private Limited and in no way they can be ousted from the affairs and management of the said Company and they have got every right to enter into the premises thereof.

The counsel for the applicant has further submitted that the order dated 22.12.2021 which has been obtained by misrepresenting the Court, deserves to be modified with liberty to the applicant and other share holders of the Company to run the affairs thereof without any hindrance and interference of the petitioners or any other person.

CRM-W 602 of 2022 is filed by four applicants namely Santosh Kumari, Meenu Chopra, Deepti Arora and Preeti Jain with a prayer for allowing them to represent before this Court so as to protect their interest in housing project namely 'Harmony Homes' which has been approved by Real Estate Regulatory Authority, Haryana and promoted by Real Height Developers Private Limited, the applicants being flat holders in the said housing project and the copy of the concerned approval is placed on record.

sentences.text: Neutral Citation No:=2023

During arguments it transpired that broadly there are three stakeholders:-
(i) petitioners Sanjay Gupta and Rajesh Gupta, who are claiming 100% ownership of Real Height Developers Private Limited;
(ii) applicant Attar Chand Gupta, his brother Shiv Charan Gupta and their sons who are also claiming share in the aforesaid Company; and (iii) allottees of the flats in Harmony Homes.
Taking note of the submissions made on behalf of the different stakeholders and in order to safeguard their interests

, the order dated 22.12.2021 is modified in the following terms:-
"That the order dated 22.12.2021 would not prejudice the rights of applicant Attar Chand Gupta, his sons Manish Mittal and Ankur Mittal, Shiv Charan Gupta and his son Parshant Kumar as well as the allottees of the flats and further should not prejudice the rights of the parties in the civil as well as criminal litigation which is already pending between stakeholders No.(i) and (ii) regarding control and management of Real Height Developers Private Limited.

Further making it clear that the order dated 22.12.2021 will be having no overriding effect on any order (including interim order) passed by any Court/ Tribunal of competent jurisdiction in due course of law, in favour of any of the stakeholders as described above.
However, the District Administration is duty bound to ensure that there is no breach of peace inside or outside the premises of the aforesaid Company and the housing project, Harmony Homes."
Both the aforesaid miscellaneous applications stand disposed of in above terms.
CRM-W-580 of 2022

This is an application moved under Section 340 Cr.P.C. by Rajesh Gupta with a prayer to hold an enquiry regarding commission of offence prescribed in Clause (b) sub Section (1)
of Section 195 Cr.P.C. in the 6 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:032479 course of proceedings carried out in CRM-W-281 of 2022 filed in CRWP No. 12055 of 2021 as well as with regard to the contents and documents produced by the applicant Attar Chand Gupta in the aforesaid application.
As per the provisions of Section 340 Cr.P.C. there are two conditions on fulfillment of which a complaint can be filed against a person who has given a false affidavit or evidence in a proceeding before a Court.

Firstly, that a person has given a false affidavit in a proceeding before the Court and secondly, in the opinion of the Court it is expedient in the interest of justice to make an enquiry against such a person in relation to the offence committed by him.
On perusal of record I do not find it expedient in the interest of justice to proceed further against the applicant Attar Chand Gupta by adopting procedure prescribed under Section 340 Cr.P.C.
The application stands disposed of accordingly.
